Merrimette, a Marine who has grown battle-scarred and disillusioned with the war, is given command of a tight-knit unit for the first time. Their assignment seems routine for a supply detachment: drive a convoy through some of the most dangerous Taliban-held territory in Helmand province to resupply a remote outpost at the edge of enemy-controlled ground. On the way, however, they are flagged down by Fox, a special operations officer who tells them their mission has changed. He is escorting Anoosh, an Afghan woman who has become famous for defying the Taliban and a symbol of resistance to them, and she must be brought to safety so she can deliver a speech at the United Nations.

The operation quickly turns into a fight for survival. Taliban forces ambush the Marines, inflicting casualties and leaving them no way back to the Green Zone except on foot, and the survivors must cross hostile country with no communication and no air support, and with only Fox's experience of the land and its people to guide them. Merrimette, whose experience until now has been limited to supply runs, must hold his unit together and protect Anoosh as they fight their way through one of the most dangerous places on Earth, while tensions flare between some of the Marines and their local allies and interpreters before giving way to mutual respect. As the Taliban close in, the Marines must rely on their courage and firepower to see Anoosh to safety, at heavy cost.

Released on home video and digital platforms in 2014, the film was followed by Jarhead 3: The Siege (2016) and Jarhead: Law of Return (2019). Common Sense Media judged it a better-than-expected war movie that conveys the Marines' esprit de corps and does not shy away from casualties, despite a formulaic story, while DVD Talk called it markedly average in concept, performances and script.

Max is a teenage stage magician who shares his home with Nicky and Tara, two young ghosts who are counting on him to help them find their missing parents. To raise money for his girlfriend Cammie's school dance crew, he stages a public séance. The ghosts supply genuine spectral effects, but everyone assumes they are Max's tricks, and when the ghost of a French maid interrupts the show with information about Nicky and Tara's parents, the evening ends in embarrassment and Cammie breaks up with him. At the same time, his ghost friends complain that he treats them more like pets than friends.

Max turns for help to Simon Drake, the self-obsessed host of a ghost-hunting television show who is filming an episode in town, only to discover that he is a fraud. The evil ghost Phears, working with the sinister Mr. Morgo, takes possession of Drake as part of a new attempt to release an army of evil spirits on the world and plunge it into darkness. The key is a dark crystal that turns up in Max's house, which Max has tried to use to win Cammie back. Hampered by fame, family squabbles, a rich rival for Cammie's affections and an anxious dance choreographer, Max has to recover the jewel and rescue Nicky and Tara before Phears succeeds, in a showdown at a derelict mansion, the Doom House of the title.

The film was released directly on DVD, digital download and on demand on 6 September 2016. Common Sense Media described it as a low-budget, harmless fright-fest with nonstop action and over-the-top villains, enlivened by Kennedy's send-up of a reality television star, but lacking in depth.

As a lonely girl in New York, Jane spends her Sundays at Tiffany's with her mother, a cold, controlling theatre producer embittered by her divorce, and brings along Michael, a boy of her own age whom only she can see. On Christmas Eve, which is also Jane's birthday, Michael explains that under the rules governing imaginary friends he must leave once she turns ten, and he vanishes from her life. Years later Jane is a successful businesswoman working alongside her mother at the theatre and is engaged to Hugh, a famous actor who seems more in love with his career than with her, with the wedding set for her birthday on Christmas Eve. Outwardly she insists that her life is perfect, but she has doubts, and her mother is more interested in controlling her than supporting her. Then Michael unexpectedly reappears, now a grown man and visible to everyone, having been summoned without her realizing it because she needs guidance. At first shocked and in denial, Jane gradually grows attached to him, rediscovering the value of simple things, while Michael adapts to the human world, finds work as a chef and begins to experience human feelings. Their friendship turns into love, and Hugh comes to see Michael as a threat. When Michael admits that the rules require him to leave her again on her birthday, the hurt Jane refuses to see him. On Christmas Eve, during the ceremony itself, she realizes her relationship with Hugh is loveless and calls off the wedding, only to find that Michael, against all expectations, has not disappeared and has become human, free to stay with her.

The film was shot in Toronto and on location between September 8 and October 1, 2010. Milano said she was drawn to the original concept and its flawed characters, and enjoyed reuniting with Winter and Sergei, with whom she had worked on Charmed. It premiered on Lifetime on December 6, 2010, drawing about 2.1 million viewers.

Dragon Ball Z: Plan to Eradicate the Super Saiyans (Japanese: Doragon Bōru: Sūpā Saiya-jin Zetsumetsu Keikaku) is a 2010 Japanese original video animation, a complete remake of a two-part 1993 OVA that had been produced as a companion to the Famicom card-battle role-playing game Dragon Ball Z Side Story: Plan to Eradicate the Saiyans, developed by Tose and published by Bandai. The voice cast is led by Masako Nozawa as Goku, Gohan and Turles, with Ryō Horikawa as Vegeta, Toshio Furukawa as Piccolo, Takeshi Kusao as Trunks, Ryūsei Nakao as Frieza and Cooler, Yusaku Yara as Lord Slug and Shinji Ogawa as the villain Dr. Raichi.

The story centres on Dr. Raichi, the last survivor of the Tuffles, a technologically advanced race that once lived on Planet Plant before it was invaded by the Saiyans. The Saiyans massacred the Tuffles, seized their technology and renamed the planet Planet Vegeta in honour of their king. Raichi escaped and took refuge on a distant dark world, where he has spent years preparing his revenge on the last remaining Saiyans.

On Earth, Raichi's devices begin releasing a substance called Destron Gas, which threatens to wipe out all life on the planet. When Mr. Popo discovers that only a few hours remain before the planet is destroyed, Goku, Gohan, Vegeta, Trunks and Piccolo race around the world to destroy the gas machines. They succeed in destroying all but one, which is protected by an impenetrable energy barrier. At that moment, some of their most dangerous past enemies, Frieza, Cooler, Turles and Lord Slug, reappear and attack them. King Kai explains that these villains are ghost warriors who will keep returning to life unless they are defeated in the same way they originally died. Tracking the source to Raichi's hideout, the heroes discover that the ghosts are generated by Hatchiyack, a machine powered by the hatred of the Tuffles, and they must face both Raichi and the monstrous power of the machine itself to save the Earth.

The story functions as a crossover that reunites the heroes with villains from several Dragon Ball Z films and story arcs, offering fans a series of rematches in a compact format.

The 1993 game on which the story is based sold around 300,000 copies in Japan and received a score of 22 out of 40 from Famitsu. Its original OVA had been released in two parts as video strategy guides, and its footage was later reused in a 1994 Playdia video game before the story was fully reanimated in 2010.

Barbie (Erica Lindbeck) and her sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea fly with their puppies Taffy, DJ, Rookie and Honey to a tropical island, where Chelsea is to compete in a dance competition against her rival, Lindsay. Chelsea wants to go straight to the hotel to rehearse, but Barbie has planned a surprise. With most rental cars taken, the sisters set off in a golf cart, send their luggage ahead and head to Banyan Tree Park for the Dancing Horse Festival, where the trainers Vivian and Marco present the nervous young horse Beauty in her debut. While the girls watch, the puppies explore a horse trailer belonging to a show dog, Archibald, and are unwittingly driven away when the trainers leave.

Trying to follow, Barbie gets the cart stuck in the arch of the great banyan tree, and with no internet signal the sisters must spend the night in the park, passing the time with imagination games and learning of a macaw constellation once used by local fishermen for navigation. The next day, finding the road washed out, they climb a mountain, take a zip-line to a village and rent a camper, only to run out of fuel near the beach campground where the trainers have stopped. Meanwhile the puppies, cared for by Vivian and Marco, enjoy their own adventure, running with the horses and learning to surf.

As her worries mount, Chelsea snaps at Barbie for being relentlessly positive, and Barbie reassures her that doing her best matters more than winning. The sisters are reunited with their pets, and when another washed-out road blocks the way, the horses carry the girls across. Barbie admits that she hid her own worries to seem dependable, and her sisters tell her she can share them. Guided north by the macaw constellation, they reach the competition. The voice cast also includes Kazumi Evans as Skipper, Claire Margaret Corlett as Stacie, Alyssya Swales as Chelsea and Mark Oliver as Archibald.

Guts is an immensely strong sword-for-hire with no direction in life beyond the next battle. When he kills an enemy champion during a siege, he draws the attention of the Band of the Hawk, a mercenary company led by the beautiful and charismatic Griffith, who defeats him in single combat and forces him to join. The relationship between the two men grows into a bond that wavers between rivalry and friendship, while Casca, the band's only woman and a tough swordswoman, struggles to accept the newcomer and his influence. Employed by the Kingdom of Midland in its Hundred Year War against the Tudor Empire, the Hawks win battle after battle, and Griffith rises steadily through the kingdom's ranks in pursuit of a mysterious, prophesied ambition. During another siege, Guts and Griffith encounter the monstrous demon Nosferatu Zodd, who notices the pendant around Griffith's neck and warns Guts that Griffith will be his doom. Griffith's rapid ascent angers Midland's noblemen, and after the king's brother, Julius, tries to have him assassinated, Griffith charges Guts with murdering Julius. Guts carries out the killing but also kills the noble's young son, an act that leaves him deeply shaken. Afterwards, he overhears Griffith say that the Hawks are his comrades, but that a true friend is someone who pursues a dream of their own rather than someone else's. The words haunt him.

The film was released in Japan by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on 4 February 2012, with a score by Shirō Sagisu and a theme by Susumu Hirasawa, and Viz Media released it on home video in North America that November. Anime News Network called it an exciting, faithful adaptation but criticized its heavy use of 3D CG animation, a complaint shared by other reviewers.

In the earlier films, Koyomi, a high school student, saved the dying Kiss-Shot by giving her his blood and was turned into her vampire servant. To become human again, he defeated the three vampire hunters, Dramaturgy, Episode and Guillotinecutter, who had cut off her limbs. With Meme's help Kiss-Shot is now fully restored, and Koyomi expects her to return his humanity. On a rooftop she tells him about her first servant, a samurai who took his own life when she could not make him human again. Returning from buying food, Koyomi finds her devouring the corpse of Guillotinecutter and is horrified to realize that she will feed on people again and that he, too, will come to crave human blood.

Despairing to the point of wanting to die, Koyomi is persuaded by Tsubasa to keep living and reminded that he alone has the power to stop Kiss-Shot. The two vampires clash in a vast, empty stadium, tearing off each other's limbs and heads only to regenerate, until Koyomi weakens her by drinking her blood. Tsubasa then realizes that Kiss-Shot wants to die: she meant to lose, since only her death can restore her servant's humanity, a sacrifice she was too afraid to make for the samurai. Unwilling to kill her, Koyomi calls on Meme, who proposes a solution that will leave everyone unhappy. Koyomi drains her blood only to the point where she is too weak to hunt humans, leaving them both caught between vampire and human. Afterwards he is mostly human with some vampire traits, while Kiss-Shot remains in the form of a child who must feed on his blood.

Reiketsu opened in Japanese cinemas on 6 January 2017, placing ninth on its opening weekend with about 86.7 million yen and earning roughly 170 million yen in four days, and it premiered in the United States on 7 April 2017. Critics, including Anime News Network, had praised the trilogy's striking animation and sound design.
